questions.q: In CRM Analytics, what powers a chart, number, or table widget on a dashboard?
options: A step, which is a query against a dataset
A live query against Salesforce objects at view time
questions.explain: Widgets are driven by steps, which are queries against datasets. Nothing queries Salesforce objects at view time.

questions.q: Which area is the operations side of CRM Analytics, where you monitor data jobs and manage pipelines?
questions.explain: Data Manager is where data jobs are monitored and recipes, dataflows, and connections are managed.

questions.q: Which statement about a CRM Analytics dataset is correct?
options: It is a standard Salesforce object visible in Object Manager
It is stored inside CRM Analytics in a compressed, indexed form and is not a Salesforce object
It is always a live view of Salesforce records
It can only contain data from one object
questions.explain: Datasets are copies prepared and stored inside CRM Analytics. They do not appear in Object Manager or native reports.

questions.q: Why does security need deliberate design on datasets?
options: Salesforce forbids more than one user
Dataset data is copied out of objects, so native record sharing does not automatically apply to it
questions.explain: Because data is copied into datasets, access must be designed for the dataset itself. Chapter 8 covers this in depth.

questions.q: A dashboard shows yesterday's numbers even though records changed this morning. Where should you look first?
options: The dataset's pipeline schedule and last run in Data Manager
questions.explain: Freshness depends on when the pipeline that builds the dataset last ran, which you can check in Data Manager's monitor view.
